messages:
tess_ml: Quick heads-up — I ran the full attention microbench after pulling latest upstreams and saw a notable throughput regression on long contexts when flash-attn is selected as the kernel.

ryan-eng: Which upstreams did we pick this morning? flash-attn tag and any vLLM/xformers patches?

tess_ml: Pulled flash-attn@v1.3.0 and xformers/vllm patches that changed kv eviction and tile heuristics. PRs: https://github.com/HazyResearch/flash-attention/pull/1501 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/702

maya_dev: Can you paste the bench command and the kernel routing config? Also did you try turning off kv cache to isolate?

tess_ml: Repro command:
```
./bench_attn --model llama-13b --seq_len 4096 --batch 8 --attn flashattn --kv_cache on --num_threads 6
```
Routing: prefer=[flashattn,fused,paged] via runtime router.

priya_perf: I ran a perf sampling on the same image. Top samples show higher time in KV reads and memcpy spikes. Quick samples: read_kv_block 31.7%, flash_attn_forward 19.8%, memcpy 14.2%

sam_rt: Interesting — flash-attn PR mentions vec4 rework and alternate blocking for large sequences; may favor latency for small batches but hurt throughput for big-kv patterns.

tess_ml: Confirmed: with kv_cache disabled throughput returns near baseline. So interaction between new FA tile sizes and our kv cache eviction pattern looks suspicious.

ryan-eng: I'll spin matrix runs (seq=1024,2048,4096 x batch=1,4,8) across old vs new FA and with/without kv cache. Expecting regressions primarily at seq>=2048 & batch>=4. ETA ~1h.

maya_dev: Can we short-circuit production for long-context requests — route seq>=2048 to paged_attn until we have root cause? I can push a canary if we agree.

ops-bot: Note: vendorZ/gpu-driver@1.0.0 dropped to staging 2025-05-12T01:05:00Z; there are kernel ABI deltas in dev notes. Might be a confounder.

priya_perf: After temporarily forcing paged_attn in my local runs, tokens/s recovers to baseline. Fused variant also fine but fused is less memory friendly.

tess_ml: Good mitigation. Action items: (1) ryan run full microbench and upload CSV + env logs; (2) maya push routing canary tag attn-fallback-canary-2025-05-12 to staging for seq>=2048 with monitoring; (3) open issue on flash-attn with perf dumps and ask about the vec4/blocking change impact on KV heavy workloads.

ryan-eng: Started runs. Will include perf maps (perf, flamegraphs) and the exact kernel build IDs.

maya_dev: Canary pushed (tag=attn-fallback-canary-2025-05-12). Monitor dashboards: per-model token throughput, p95 latency, and KV read rate. Please watch for tail latency spikes.

sam_rt: I propose also adding a small synthetic that simulates eviction churn (move eviction threshold from 0.5->0.7 in vLLM patch apparently) to see if vLLM change alone causes the extra KV reads.

tess_ml: Agreed. Also filing upstream issue to flash-attn maintainers referencing our perf traces and asking if we can opt into legacy blocking for large-seq builds.

priya_perf: FYI, if this is due to tile dims, we might be able to add a kernel selector that prefers fused/paged when avg_seq_length > 1024 and batch>2 as an automated rule until upstream lands a fix.

ci-bot: CI note: running GPU compatibility tests against vendorZ/gpu-driver@1.0.0 in staging; will report regressions to #eng-infra.

tess_ml: Thanks all. We'll hold the paged fallback for ~48h during investigation and upstream triage. If ryan's matrix shows anything surprising post-driver drop I'll post updates here.

ryan-eng: Uploading initial CSV and flamegraphs to the perf bucket now (link coming). ETA ~15m.

maya_dev: Also logging a runtime config change so we can revert the canary cleanly.

sam_rt: I'll sketch an adaptive router that samples recent seq/batch distribution and picks kernels dynamically; can iterate once we have stable metrics.

priya_perf: Great, thanks. If upstream responds quickly we can try a patched FA build in staging tomorrow.

tess_ml: OK team — standup sync will cover any visible canary signals. Ping me if you see >5% regressions on any model. :)
